subject: Cascade County — Fed-adjacent privacy annex + evidence request
messages:
From: Emily Hart <emily.hart@cascadecounty.gov>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@cascadecounty.gov>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cascade County RFP — privacy annex / evidence request

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week. Cascade County is moving quickly through procurement and our legal team flagged a few items we need to validate before the IT Board signs off. Can you provide the following as part of the privacy and security package?

- Your latest SOC 2 Type II attestation and monitoring period.
- A completed CAIQ / SIG-lite questionnaire (we only need the CAIQ sections relevant to FedRAMP-adjacent controls).
- A brief DPIA summary showing data flows for county PII and any mitigations (high level is fine).
- Confirmation you will accept our Privacy Annex with the following changes: data residency (US-only), SCCs where applicable, and a 3-year retention default with county-controlled deletion rights.
- Evidence of encryption at rest + KMS/HSM approach and whether keys are customer-managed or provider-managed.
- A pointer to quarterly penetration test reports or summary.

We are on a tight schedule and would appreciate a response by COB Friday (2026-11-13). If some items need legal review, an acknowledgement with ETA is fine.

Thanks,
Emily Hart
Procurement Manager
Cascade County

[Attachment: RFP_Privacy_Annex_Draft_v4.pdf (reference only)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@cascadecounty.gov>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cascade County RFP — privacy annex / evidence request

Hi Emily — thanks, and great to be moving forward. A quick acknowledgment and initial package attached; I looped in Legal (Lauren) and Security (Mina) for the annex and technical evidence.

Attached: SOC2_Type2_2026Q3.pdf (attestation stub), SIG_CAIC_20261111.xlsx (completed CAIQ mappings), DPIA_Summary_Cascade_20261111.docx (high-level DPIA).

Quick answers up front:
- SOC 2: Type II, coverage period 2026-04-01 to 2026-09-30.
- CAIQ: completed with notes on FedRAMP-adjacent controls — see tab "FedAdjNotes".
- DPIA summary: contains top-level dataflow diagram, PII categories, and mitigations (KV cache policies, token redaction, retention controls).
- Data residency: Redwood offers US-only regions and can pin tenant data to us-west-1 or us-east-1; we can confirm region during onboarding.
- SCCs / DPA: Redwood's standard DPA references SCCs where applicable; Lauren (cc) will confirm acceptance of your annex redlines.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest; customer KMS integration via AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault supported. By default keys are provider-managed; we offer customer-managed keys on Dedicated/Private plans.
- Pen tests: we provide quarterly summary reports; full reports are available under NDA.

ETA: Lauren and Mina — can you review the county changes to the Privacy Annex and confirm which items are require legal escalation? Emily, if anything in the attachments is missing or you need a specific evidence format (e.g., .xlsx CAIQ vs. SIG), let me know and we'll prioritize.

Proposed timeline: preliminary evidence sent now; legal decision on annex by 2026-11-17; final DocuSign by 2026-11-24.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

[Attachments: SOC2_Type2_2026Q3.pdf, SIG_CAIC_20261111.xlsx, DPIA_Summary_Cascade_20261111.docx]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Cascade County RFP — privacy annex / evidence request

Aditya / Mina — I reviewed Emily's draft annex and made inline comments. High-level guidance:

1) Data residency: agreeable — we can commit to US-only region for this contract (pin at onboarding).
2) SCCs: we accept incorporation of SCCs where applicable for cross-border transfers, but note Redwood's standard DPA already maps to SCCs; we will not sign alternate SCC language that imposes additional audit obligations beyond our standard SOC2 & audit scopes.
3) 3-year retention default: acceptable as default, but any modifications that require permanent deletion of audit logs or system telemetry are not acceptable; propose "customer data" retained per annex but system logs retained for a minimum of 24 months for security investigations.
4) Customer-managed keys: for Dedicated/Private deployments we can offer CMK via AWS KMS; Hosted plans remain provider-managed unless customer upgrades.
5) Pen tests: we can provide a redacted quarterly penetration test summary; full reports require NDA.

Action: Aditya, send Emily the proposed annex with tracked changes and a DocuSign envelope. Mina — can you attach the redacted pen test summary and confirm the CAIQ annotations?

Lauren Bishop
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

[Internal note: avoid accepting any clause that mandates in-person audits or non-standard log deletion windows.]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@cascadecounty.gov>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cascade County RFP — privacy annex / evidence request

Emily — thanks for the list. Per Lauren's guidance, please find the following items attached and a short technical note below.

Attachments included: redacted_pen_test_summary_2026Q3.pdf (summary), SIG_CAIC_20261111.xlsx (CAIQ with cell-level notes), DPIA_Summary_Cascade_20261111.docx.

Technical notes:
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit. For Hosted we use provider-managed keys (AWS KMS multi-tenant) with strict key access controls. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys.
- Key management and separation: KMS access is restricted via IAM roles scoped to the tenant. We log KMS API calls in our audit trail and retain KMS logs for 12 months by default (extendable under contract).
- Logs & audit trails: Token-level request logs, model route traces, and denial/error logs are stored in encrypted archives; access requires RBAC and is logged via SIEM.
- DPIA: DPIA summary includes mitigations such as prefix caching minimization for PII-heavy routes, prompt redaction guidance, and recommended retention configurations.

If the county requires CMK for the hosted offering specifically, that will require a Dedicated engagement; happy to scope if that's the path.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

[Attachments: redacted_pen_test_summary_2026Q3.pdf, SIG_CAIC_20261111.xlsx, DPIA_Summary_Cascade_20261111.docx]

From: Emily Hart <emily.hart@cascadecounty.gov>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cascade County RFP — privacy annex / evidence request

Aditya / Lauren / Mina — thank you for the quick turnaround and the materials. Cascade County legal reviewed the attachments and had two final asks before we circulate to the IT Board next week:

1) Can Redwood provide a redacted executive summary of the most recent penetration test that includes severity levels and remediation status? The summary you sent is a good start but the Board wants the severity table visible (we understand full reports require an NDA).
2) We need explicit confirmation that Redwood will sign the county's Privacy Annex with the agreed changes Lauren outlined: US-only region pin, SCCs incorporated where required, and 3-year retention for customer data (with the 24-month minimum for security logs). Please confirm acceptance in email form for our procurement file.

If you can confirm both items and provide the DocuSign link for signature by COB Wednesday (2026-11-24), we can move to final approval. Appreciate the responsiveness.

Best,
Emily Hart
Procurement Manager
Cascade County
